stem.text: Explain the use of genes for fluorescence as markers in gene technology.

points.text: add marker gene to the, vector / plasmid ;
gene of interest inserted close to marker gene ;
(marker) gene product / protein, emits light ;
visible colour change ;
ref. to exposing to UV light / laser scanner ;
easy to identify transformed, bacteria / organisms ;
examples ; e.g. GFP
idea of no known risk ;
AVP ; e.g. ref. to gene of interest inserted into marker gene / insertional inactivation

explanation.text: A fluorescent marker provides a detectable product linked to the introduced DNA. Explain how this connection allows transformed organisms to be identified, rather than merely naming a fluorescent protein.

reasoningChain: Link the marker gene with the vector and gene of interest.
Describe production and detection of the fluorescent protein.
Explain the identification of transformed cells or organisms.

issues.note: 与Q10二选一，各15分。两题均收录，全部题分115，paper保持100并由optionalGroups计算选答。

bullets: Candidates needed to explain the use of genes for fluorescence as markers in gene technology. Most candidates provided an answer that lacked detail. The most common points covered were the use of UV light and how fluorescence indicated that the organism contained recombinant DNA. Improvements could have been made in examination technique by giving more carefully ordered and detailed responses.

Candidates achieved higher credit on this part of the question discussing the social implications of using genetically modified organisms in food production. The most commonly seen creditworthy points were the identification of disadvantages like consumer resistance to GM crops, safety aspects for humans, as well as it being expensive. A few candidates were able to discuss some positive aspects, for example, an increase in yield or improved food quality.
